L390: The fallback value allows for some types of defensive coding. For example, an author may create a component intended to be included in a larger application, and use variables to style it so that it’s easy for the author of the larger application to theme the component to match the rest of the app.
L391: Without fallback, the app author must supply a value for every variable that your component uses. With fallback, the component author can supply defaults, so the app author only needs to supply values for the variables they wish to override.

L395:       color: var(--header-color, blue);
L396:     }
L397:     .component .text {
L398:       color: var(--text-color, black);
L399:     }
L400: 
L401:     /* In the larger application's style: */
L402:     .component {
L403:       --text-color: #080;
L404:       /* header-color isn't set,
L405:          and so remains blue,
L406:          the fallback value */
L407:     }
L408: To cite577†replace a var() function , given a list of `arguments`:
L409: 
L410:   1. Let `el` be the element that the style containing the cite55†var() function is being applied to. Let `first arg` be the first cite63†<declaration-value> in `arguments`. Let `second arg` be the <declaration-value>? passed after the comma, or null if there was no comma.
L411:   2. cite61†Substitute arbitrary substitution functions in `first arg`, then cite578†parse it as a cite276†<custom-property-name> . If parsing returned a <custom-property-name>, let `result` be the cite271†computed value of the corresponding cite54†custom property on `el`. Otherwise, let `result` be the cite66†guaranteed-invalid value .
L412: 
L413: Note: Determining the cite271†computed value for the cite54†custom property implies that cite579†property replacement takes place, which may cause a cite580†cycle .
L414:   3. If the cite54†custom property named by the cite55†var() ’s first argument is cite227†animation-tainted , and the var() is being used in a property that is cite581†not animatable , set `result` to the cite66†guaranteed-invalid value .
L415: 
L416:   4. If `result` contains the cite66†guaranteed-invalid value , and `second arg` was provided, set `result` to the result of cite61†substitute arbitrary substitution functions on `second arg`.
L417: 
L418:   5. Return `result`.
L419: Due to cite579†property replacement , cite54†custom properties can form cite580†cycles :
L420: 
L421:     :root {
L422:       --one: calc(var(--two) + 20px);
L423:       --two: calc(var(--one) - 20px);
L424:     }
L425: 
L426: 
L427: In the above, both --one and --two compute to the cite66†guaranteed-invalid value , since their cite582†substitution contexts have been marked as cyclic.

L447: 
L448: All cite54†custom property cite601†declarations have the cite602†case-sensitive flag set.

L455: ### 4.1. Serializing Custom Properties
L456: 
L457: Custom property names must be serialized as the exact code point sequence provided by the author, including not altering the case.
L458: 
L459: Note: For non-custom properties, property names are restricted to the ASCII range and are cite108†ASCII case-insensitive†infra.spec.whatwg.org , so implementations typically serialize the name lowercased.
L460: Specified values of cite54†custom properties must be serialized exactly as specified by the author (with one exception, below). Simplifications that might occur in other properties, such as dropping comments, normalizing whitespace, reserializing numeric tokens from their value, etc., must not occur.
L461: 
L462: Computed values of cite54†custom properties must similarly be serialized exactly as specified by the author (with the same one exception, below), save for the replacement of any cite55†var() functions.
L463: The one exception to serialization being precisely as specified in the source file is that an empty custom property (such as --foo:;) must serialize with a single space as its value.
L464: 
L465: Tests
L466: 
L467:   * cite610†variable-reference-shorthands-cssom.html†wpt.fyi cite611†(live test)†wpt.live cite612†(source)†github.com L468:   * cite613†variable-reference-variable.html†wpt.fyi cite614†(live test)†wpt.live cite615†(source)†github.com L469: For example, given the following properties:
L470: 
L471:     --y: /* baz */;
L472:     --x: /* foo */ var(--y) /* bar */;
L473: 
L474: 
L475: the serialization of the specified value of --x must be `"/* foo */ var(--y) /* bar */"`, while the serialization of the computed value of --x must be `"/* foo */ /* baz */ /* bar */"`.
L476: 
L477: (Note that the leading whitespace on the value is automatically trimmed by the CSS parser; it’s not preserved here.)
L478: This "exactly as specified" requirement exists because authors sometimes store non-CSS information in custom properties, and "normalizing" this information can change it in ways that break author code.
L479: 
L480: For example, storing a UUID in a custom property, like --uuid: 12345678-12e3-8d9b-a456-426614174000, requires the UUID to be echoed back out as written when it’s accessed by script.
L481: This value is technically parsed by CSS as a series of adjacent numbers and dimensions. In particular, the segment "-12e3" parses as a number, equal to -12000. Reserializing it in that form, as required by CSSOM in other contexts, would fatally break the author’s use of the value.
L482: The requirement to serialize an empty custom property as a string with a single space in it instead is due to compatibility with the existing CSSOM API. `cite616†setProperty() ` specifies that if the passed value is an empty string it instead acts as `cite617†removeProperty() `.
L483: This is a frankly weird behavior, and not something we would do in new APIs. But we can’t change the past, and letting empty properties accurately serialize as the empty string would mean that round-tripping a custom property value, or reading a property on one element and setting a property on another element to the same value, wouldn’t work as intended.
L484: Using a single space preserves the author-intended behavior as much as possible, while having the smallest chance of accidentally breaking things, since authors working with custom property values in JS are probably calling `cite618†trim()†tc39.es ` on the values anyway.
L485: ## 5. Changes
L486: 
L487: ### 5.1. Changes Since the 16 June 2022 CR Snapshot
L488: 
L489:   * Clarified that the comment-insertion can happen with 0+ comments between the original tokens, not just exactly 1.
L490: 
L491:   * Clarified the transition behavior of custom properties, in a note
L492: 
L493:   * Made cite55†var() short-circuiting. (cite619†Issue 11500†github.com )
L494: ### 5.2. Changes Since the 11 November 2021 CR Draft
L495: 
L496:   * Clarified that custom properties apply all pseudo-elements (including those with restricted property lists)
L497: 
L498:   * Added example to illustrate issues with combining characters, ligatures, etc
L499: 
L500:   * Strengthened wording around similar-appearing variable names that use distinct codepoint sequences
L501: 
L502:   * Clarified an example by using more visually distinct languages as examples (English and Greek)
L503: 
L504:   * Split Security and Privacy into separate sections
L505: ### 5.3. Changes Since the 03 December 2015 CR
L506: 
L507:   * Now that cite620†[css-syntax-3] auto-trims whitespace from declaration values, made cite63†<declaration-value> optional in the custom property grammar, so that empty variables are still allowed. (cite621†Issue 774†github.com )
L508: 
L509:   * Similarly, made empty fallbacks valid in cite55†var() .
L510: 
L511:   * The -- property is reserved for future use by CSS.
L512:   * Added concept of "animation-tainted", to prevent non-animatable properties from using a variable to smuggle in some animatability.
L513: 
L514:   * Defined the cite66†guaranteed-invalid value to make the initial value of custom properties and the result of cycles or substitution failure more straightforward, and allow failure to propagate thru substitutions until finally intercepted by a fallback.
L515: 
L516:   * Defined that cycles trigger cite272†invalid at computed-value time behavior.
L517:   * Allowed variables to resolve to a CSS-wide keyword (only possible by providing it as a fallback).
L518: 
L519:   * Clarified that cite226†registered custom properties†drafts.css-houdini.org act like non-custom properties when they’re cite272†invalid at computed-value time .
L520: 
L521:   * Made longhands with cite55†var() s also trigger their shorthands to be unserializable, like longhands with pending-substitution values already did.
L522: 
L523:   * Required UAs to defend against exponential substitution attacks.
L524:   * Defined how to serialize the values of custom properties (previously, only the property name’s serialization was specified).
L525: ### 5.4. Changes since the May 6 2014 Last Call Working Draft
L526: 
L527:   * Serialization of longhands when shorthand uses a variable was defined.
L528: 
L529:   * Link to DOM’s definition of "case-sensitive".
L530: 
L531:   * Added example of using variables with cite622†:lang() to do simple i18n.
L532: 
L533:   * Clarified that usage of cite55†var() in a custom property must be valid per the var() grammar.
L534: ## 6. Acknowledgments
L535: 
L536: Many thanks to several people in the CSS Working Group for keeping the dream of variables alive over the years, particularly Daniel Glazman and David Hyatt. Thanks to multiple people on the mailing list for helping contribute to the development of this incarnation of variables, particularly Brian Kardell, David Baron, François Remy, Roland Steiner, and Shane Stephens.
L537: ## 7. Privacy Considerations
L538: 
L539: This specification defines a purely author-level mechanism for passing styling information around within a page they control. As such, there are no new privacy considerations.
L540: ## 8. Security Considerations
